name: Toggle group
purpose: Keep a button pressed until it is pressed again, such as turning on bold, in a group that shares one value.

notFor.when: The arrow keys should select an option as they move, or it is one form choice.
The user picks several choices in a form.

basis.note: Behaviors come from the Notion UI SDK inventory (2026-11-21). The support tag on each one was checked against the Radix source on the checked date. The Notion Toggle page also covers a single Toggle. Those lines are left out, because there is no vois-toggle item yet.

anatomy.note: Holds the value. type is single or multiple.
One toggle. Give each a unique value. An icon-only item needs an aria-label.
Notion names it. Radix has no such part. Hide the icon from screen readers yourself.

behaviors.text: Pressing a toggle switches it between pressed and unpressed. Its label stays the same in both states.
behaviors.evidence: toggle.tsx: onClick sets pressed to the opposite and aria-pressed follows it
behaviors.note: Keeping the label fixed is up to the author.

behaviors.text: Pressing it never submits a form.
In a group, pressing one toggle unpresses the others. Pressing the pressed one again clears the selection.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: type=single holds one string value; pressing the pressed item sends an empty value

behaviors.text: A group can be set to always keep one toggle pressed.
behaviors.note: Radix has no such prop. Ignore the empty value in onValueChange, as vois-segmented-control does.

behaviors.text: A group can allow several toggles to stay pressed at once.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: type=multiple holds an array of values

behaviors.text: In a group, the toggles' own pressed state does not apply, because the group owns which ones are pressed.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: ToggleGroupItemProps omits pressed and computes it from the group value

behaviors.text: A change can be cancelled from its callback, so the current state is kept.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: value and onValueChange through useControllableState; the callback has no cancel
behaviors.note: Use a controlled value and do not update it.

behaviors.text: A controller can change a group's value from anywhere, such as from a keyboard shortcut.
behaviors.note: Radix has no shortcut part. Add the key handler yourself.

behaviors.text: Enter or Space presses or unpresses the focused toggle.
behaviors.evidence: toggle.tsx: the toggle is a button and onClick toggles it

behaviors.text: In a group, Left and Right move focus in a horizontal group, and Up and Down move focus in a vertical group, without changing which toggles are pressed.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: orientation is passed to RovingFocusGroup
behaviors.note: vois-toggle-group draws a horizontal group only. A vertical group needs its own edge and corner rules.

behaviors.text: Home moves focus to the first toggle and End moves it to the last.
behaviors.evidence: roving-focus-group.tsx: MAP_KEY_TO_FOCUS_INTENT maps Home and PageUp to first, End and PageDown to last

behaviors.text: Arrow keys wrap from the last toggle to the first by default, or can be set to stop at the ends.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: loop defaults to true and goes to RovingFocusGroup

behaviors.text: In right-to-left text, Left and Right swap.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: dir goes to RovingFocusGroup through useDirection
behaviors.note: Pass dir for right-to-left pages. Whether the group reads the page's own direction is not checked.

behaviors.text: A group has one tab stop. It enters on the first enabled pressed toggle, or the first enabled toggle, and later returns to the toggle focused last.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: items pass active={pressed} to the roving focus group; roving-focus-group.tsx keeps one tab stop

behaviors.text: A toggle can start pressed.
In a group, disabled toggles stay reachable with the arrow keys, are reported as disabled, and ignore presses.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: the item passes focusable={!disabled}, so roving focus skips it
behaviors.note: Arrow keys skip disabled toggles. This is the same as Tabs. Decide if that is acceptable. If not, build the focus rule yourself.

behaviors.text: A disabled toggle can be kept focusable, still ignoring presses, with an explanation of why it is unavailable.
behaviors.note: Radix does not support this. Use aria-disabled and block the press yourself.

behaviors.text: A disabled toggle can still start pressed, and a surrounding fieldset disables it too.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: pressed comes from the group value whether or not the item is disabled; a disabled fieldset disables the button elements inside it

behaviors.text: Toggles do not submit values, so a group kept in a form needs its value copied into hidden fields by hand.
behaviors.note: Radix has no form value for a toggle group.

behaviors.text: A toggle is a native button that reports whether it is pressed, so screen readers announce the state while the label stays unchanged.
behaviors.evidence: toggle.tsx: aria-pressed on a button; toggle-group.tsx: only type=single replaces it with role=radio and aria-checked
behaviors.note: True for type=multiple. A type=single group announces radios, not toggles. See the group role line.

behaviors.text: An icon-only toggle needs an accessible label, and an icon inside a toggle is hidden from screen readers.
behaviors.note: vois-toggle-group sets neither. Add aria-label to the item and aria-hidden to the icon.

behaviors.text: A group has the group role rather than toolbar or radio group, so it can sit inside a toolbar, and its toggles remain buttons.
behaviors.evidence: toggle-group.tsx: type=single renders role=radiogroup with role=radio items; type=multiple renders role=toolbar
behaviors.note: Radix gives a single group radio roles and a multiple group the toolbar role. Listen to a screen reader before you ship. Decide if radio or toolbar is acceptable.

mistakes.text: Do not change the label between pressed and unpressed. Keep the label the same in both states.
Do not use a toggle group where the arrow keys should select an option as they move. Use a radio group, because a toggle group moves focus first and waits for a press.
Do not rely on toggles to submit form values. Copy a toggle group's value into hidden inputs yourself if you keep it in a form.
